newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit still has work to do before taking office.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit still has work to do before taking office.

text.p: Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has been named Thailand's new prime minister but he and his five coalition partners must decide how to share out cabinet posts before they can take office, party officials said on Tuesday.

Chavalit, the leader of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) which won the most seats in last week's general election, was officially named the 22nd prime minister by a royal decree issued by King Bhumibol Adulyadej on Monday.
Chavalit has formed a six-party coalition that will command a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-member parliament.
But he and his partners must end their wrangling over how to share out the various ministries before the king will allow them to take office, government officials said.
Members of the coalition parties said negotiations on the portfolios were continuing on Tuesday.
"We are still working on allocating some of the ministries," said Suvat Liptapanlop, secretary general of the Chart Pattana party, the second largest coalition member.
"We have reached a common view on some ministries but on others there is still more to discuss," he said.
Officials expect the cabinet list to be finalised and presented to the king within the next few days. The government is due to be sworn in around December 1.
Most of the delay has been caused by discussions between the NAP and Chart Pattana over how to divide up the economic portfolios.
Both parties vowed during the election campaign to give priority to improving Thailand's sagging economy, if elected.
Chavalit favours naming respected banker and former foreign minister Amnuay Viravan finance minister and deputy prime minister in charge of all economic issues.
The two have suggested naming a team of unelected experts to form an economic advisory team to help resuscitate the economy which this year has been growing at its slowest pace in a decade.
But Chart Pattana leader and former premier Chatichai Choonhavan has said his party has several capable elected politicians who could do the job.
Chavalit will meet visiting U.S. president Bill Clinton on Tuesday.

Clinton, on a brief visit to Bangkok following the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in the Philippines, on Tuesday morning met caretaker premier Banharn Silpa-archa to discuss commercial and security issues.
Chavalit and Clinton were expected to hold similar discussions at a meeting on Tuesday afternoon, U.S. and Thai officials said.
